name: Zelophehad
overview: Zelophehad is a female figure mentioned in 1 Chronicles 7:15 as the second wife of Machir. There is some uncertainty whether she is the second wife or possibly the second sister of Machir's wife. Beyond this unique attribute, Scripture provides no further details about her tribe or additional notes.
namesAndTitles: The name Zelophehad means 'shadow of dread' or 'terror,' which can also be understood as 'protection from terror or dread.' This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 7:15, is not indicated to have been given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Zelophehad is explicitly identified as the wife of Machir according to 1 Chronicles 7:15. Scripture does not record any other family relationships for her beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Zelophehad's significance in the biblical narrative is primarily tied to her marital relationship with Machir as noted in 1 Chronicles 7:15. While little else is recorded about her, her mention preserves the lineage and family connections important to the genealogical records of Israel. Her name, carrying a meaning related to protection from terror, also reflects the rich depth of biblical names.
